The year is this page's (re-opened 2026-10-19); the rattanakosin-kingdom dossier dates the same relation 1786 ('Siam only resumed real political control over the Northern Malay sultanates in 1786', Thonburi Kingdom page) under the string 'Terengganu', and the page here has no 1786: the disagreement goes to se-01. The region is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 9 July 1909: Siam's suzerainty over Terengganu ends. The treaty 'was signed on 10 March 1909 in Bangkok, with ratifications exchanged in London on 9 July 1909'; Article 1 transfers Siamese rights over 'the states of Kelantan, Tringganu, Kedah, Perlis, and adjacent islands' to Britain. The dissolve below passes the sultanate to the British protectorate.

region.text: Terengganu, 'Tringganu' in Article 1 of the treaty

ledger.note: 1909: Siam passes Terengganu to Britain. The treaty 'was signed on 10 March 1909 in Bangkok, with ratifications exchanged in London on 9 July 1909'; Article 1 transfers Siamese rights over 'the states of Kelantan, Tringganu, Kedah, Perlis, and adjacent islands', which 'entered the British sphere of influence as protectorates'. The Sultan of Terengganu page: 'Under his reign Terengganu became a British protectorate via the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909.' Dated to the ratification in July, as the Kedah and Rattanakosin dossiers do.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line for Terengganu's borders with Kelantan, Pahang or Patani appears on the pages opened; the 1909 treaty transfers suzerainty, not frontiers.

notes:
Page budget 1-2: two pages opened. The ledger is short because the pages hold no other dated change in Terengganu's land. (1) Suzerainty (the Siamese vassal pair is now in this ledger, see REVISION below): the first page says 'In 1741, Sultan Sulaiman of Johor appointed Sultan Mansur as the ruler of Terengganu' and 'In 1871, Terengganu became a vassal state of the Thai Rattanakosin Kingdom, and sent tribute every year called bunga mas'; the Anglo-Siamese page says the 1826 Burney Treaty 'affirmed British assent that Kedah, Perlis, Terengganu and Patani were Thai provinces'. The rattanakosin-kingdom dossier (se-02) dates the vassalage 1786-1909 (counterpart written 'Terengganu', not the slug), which conflicts with the 1871 on this page. The Johor dossier mentions the 1741 appointment only in the note of its 1722 loss, with no vassal event. (2) Cliopatria's row ends in 1904 but the sovereignty ends on 9 July 1909; two keyframes (1722-1726, 1905-1909) extend the outline. (3) The sultanate continues after 1909 as a protectorate, with a constitution in 1911, a British adviser in 1919, uprisings in 1922, 1925 and 1928, a Japanese-appointed sultan 1942-1945 and Thai administration from 1943 (page); none of that is drawn here. (4) Page discrepancies: the rulers' bullet list gives Ismail Nasiruddin 1965-1970 while the table gives 1945-1979; the infobox age is out of date. (5) No war is dated on the pages, so wars is empty. (6) Capital: Kuala Terengganu inferred, see capitals. Neighbours in the seed: Kelantan (from 1762) and Pahang (from 1853) have dossiers from other batches.

REVISION 2026-10-19 (after review): added vassal_start 1871 and vassal_end 1909-7, counterpart rattanakosin-kingdom, because rule 4 puts both sides of a vassalage in the ledger; I had left them to Siam's dossier. Page re-opened: Sultan of Terengganu ('In 1871, Terengganu became a vassal state of the Thai Rattanakosin Kingdom, and sent tribute every year called bunga mas.'; the page has no 1786, no area). Start year is 1871 (confidence 2) against 1786 in rattanakosin-kingdom /ledger/8 (Thonburi Kingdom page, counterpart string 'Terengganu'); I did not open a page that settles it and se-01 should. The vassal pair is written with counterpart = the suzerain (rattanakosin-kingdom), as the reviewer asked; the schema text puts the vassal's name in the suzerain's event, so Siam's pair (counterpart 'Terengganu') and this one mirror each other. Thin points left: the sultanate continues as a British protectorate after 1909 (adviser 1919) and is not drawn; a project-wide rule for protected states is needed (Brunei runs to 2024 with a rename in 1888); I did not open Unfederated Malay States or Terengganu pages (budget 1-2 pages, one re-opened). Capital Kuala Terengganu remains the researcher's reading (confidence 2).
